name: Isebe
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: No grammar, phonology, or sketch of Isebe (Madang) located online

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp.
sources.note: pp. 13-14: identical sentence -- stress marking omitted because stress patterning not yet established. Thesis version of the 1971 book; nothing Isebe-specific on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page iseb1246 (Hammarstrom et al.)
sources.note: Bibliography = Z'graggen 1969/1975/1980 plus classification/Ethnologue refs; no grammar, sketch or phonology listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
The single inventory linked to iseb1246 is 'Ngomba (PH 962)', a Grassfields language -- a mis-link, not Isebe; irrelevant.
Lexicon from Z'graggen (1980) only; no other source; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Roberts, John R. 1991. A study of the dialects of Amele. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 22: 67-126.
sources.note: Uses Isebe forms from Z'graggen 1980 for consonant correspondences across the Gum languages (fn. 7, Tables 13-17); says nothing about Isebe stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. xvi+199 pp. (Isebe = language C7).
sources.note: Introduction sec. 6 (pp. viii-x) describes a semi-phonemic transcription and lists fluctuating sounds (Isebe: y~z~Z, l~r); no statement on stress and the ~300 Isebe forms carry no stress marks. Sec. 2 notes Panim and Isebe share >80% vocabulary.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Classification and population only (Gum Family incl. Isebe, C7 Isebe 845 speakers); nothing on stress or Isebe phonology.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Sec. 1.3.3, p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' -- a blanket statement for all languages of the survey. Isebe entry (2.21.11.11, p. 25) gives villages and earlier mentions only; Mabuso Stock typology (2.21.16) and Madang Phylum typology (2.21.5) list segment inventories, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Isebe language'; Ethnologue free page igo (via r.jina.ai)
Pawley, Andrew. 2006. Madang languages. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed., vol. 7, 429-432. Oxford: Elsevier.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Family overview that may carry a general remark on prosody in Madang languages (second-hand at best).
sources.venue: Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed

sources.citation: Roberts, John R. 1987. Amele. (Croom Helm Descriptive Grammars.) London: Croom Helm. [sister Gum language]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Closest fully described relative (Gum family); its stress statement is the only family-internal comparandum, usable for a hedged family-level note but not for Isebe itself.
sources.venue: (Croom Helm Descriptive Grammars.) London: Croom Helm. [sister Gum language]

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John (collector). 1970-73. Madang Province field recordings and word-list notebooks (Isebe list C7), PARADISEC collections JZ1/JZ2 and Anthropos Institute papers
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Primary audio of the Isebe 300-item list; the only material from which Isebe stress could be established instrumentally, since Z'graggen himself left stress unmarked.

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1905. Beitrage zur Kenntnis der Sprachen von Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen des Seminars fur Orientalische Sprachen 8: 182-254 (Panim-village word list, p. 245, = first Isebe list per Z'graggen 1971: 25)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Oldest Isebe word list; German-era lists sometimes carry acute accents marking stress, which would be the only first-hand stress evidence in print.
sources.venue: Mitteilungen des Seminars fur Orientalische Sprachen
